annotations.description:
Over the last hour, {{ $values.C.Value | humanizePercentage }} of the {{ $values.B.Value }} {{ $labels.platform }} jobs that were not held by their account's concurrency limit waited more than 10 s for the runner that ran them, so the p90 queue time is over the 10 s target. It has stayed there for 30 minutes.

Queue time is what the runners dashboard reports: enqueue to the claim of the runner GitHub ran the job on (`executor_claimed_at`). A job counts as held, and is left out, when its account's open runner sessions plus the job exceeded the account's limit at enqueue or 15 s before that claim.

First query (Prometheus, grafanacloud-prom): 1 - sum by (fleet) (increase(tuist_runners_job_executor_queue_time_milliseconds_bucket{env="production", platform="{{ $labels.platform }}", limit_held="false", le="10000.0"}[1h])) / sum by (fleet) (increase(tuist_runners_job_executor_queue_time_milliseconds_count{env="production", platform="{{ $labels.platform }}", limit_held="false"}[1h])) names the pools.

Likely causes:
- The pool had no warm runner, so jobs waited for a cold boot (a median 20 to 26 s on the rack, 13 to 16 s on Linux). Compare tuist_runners_autoscaler_learned_warm_floor_replicas and tuist_runners_autoscaler_warm_deficit_replicas for the pool.
- A fan-out larger than the pool's floor.
- The fleet is out of capacity: check Runner fleet out of macOS capacity and Runner jobs waiting for a runner.
- Re-queued jobs after the runner shuffle (tuist_runners_job_requeued_count).
